RESULT [labelnoise]: Table 2: a unified detector trained without pseudo-labelling scored 36.5 AP on the VOC-on-COCO evaluation, against 62.2 with their pseudo-labelling (MIX: 43.7 vs 52.2). Partial-loss variants alone (36.1-39.2) did not close the gap.
US [labelnoise]: Harvested weed datasets usually label one or a few species (or just 'weed'), so other cwd12 species visible in those images become false background once merged. The trainer should pseudo-label or loss-mask absent classes per source dataset, not merge naively. Naive merging is a plausible silent cause of mAP drops after an increment.
CORRECTION [labelnoise]: Table 2 is verified. Unify w/o Pseudo-Labeling scores 36.5 on V-on-C and 43.7 on MIX, against 62.2 and 52.2 for Pseudo-Labeling. The partial-loss variants score 36.1-39.2 on V-on-C.
